channel.title: Acting UK Industry News
channel.description: Acting UK Industry News — original editorial coverage for UK actors.

item.title: The BFI backs a more thoughtful approach to screen technology
item.description: New funding for NFTS and Falmouth aims to help independent filmmakers work with emerging technology without losing sight of the people involved.

item.title: Equity's AI deal gives performers a vote on their digital doubles
item.description: A proposed three-year Equity–Pact agreement promises new safeguards for performers’ likenesses, self-tapes and pay. Members now decide whether to accept it.

item.title: Hamnet leaves Stratford for its first UK tour
item.description: The RSC and Neal Street stage adaptation will begin a nationwide tour in Salford in September 2027, with casting still to come.

item.title: Rambert takes It’s a Sin back to the dancefloor
item.description: A new trailer offers a first look at the dance adaptation of Russell T Davies’s television drama, ahead of its Manchester premiere.

item.title: Matt Henry takes the classroom in To Sir, With Love
item.description: The Olivier Award-winning performer leads a new musical adaptation touring the UK from April 2027.

item.title: Edinburgh Fringe raises the price of taking a chance
item.description: The Fringe Society has announced higher show registration fees for 2027, ending a freeze that began in 2007.

item.title: The National Theatre takes its name seriously
item.description: A four-year programme backed by up to £15 million aims to bring theatre and creative training to more than 100,000 young people across England.

item.title: The Yard makes room for Sondheim
item.description: Jay Miller will direct the Hackney Wick theatre’s first musical, Company, ahead of a transfer to Theatr Clwyd and a national tour.

item.title: Barbara Broccoli takes the helm at the NFTS
item.description: The Bond producer becomes the National Film and Television School’s first woman president, as the school prepares to open a new building in January.

item.title: Bectu renews its call for safer creative workplaces
item.description: The union is urging employers to implement the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority’s framework, with particular attention to reporting concerns.

item.title: The Old Vic opens a new chapter with Rupert Goold’s first season
item.description: Four productions lead the incoming artistic director’s 2027 programme, with public booking due to open on 16 November.

item.title: Bradford venue faces closure
item.description: Theatre in the Mill is due to close on 31 March 2027.

item.title: Spotlight fees are heading back to court. What does it mean for actors?
item.description: Equity’s appeal is set for 24 November. Here is what is at stake for working actors.

item.title: The UK screen sector in numbers
item.description: A briefing on the BFI’s latest quarterly figures.
